comparator.route: Track Geschiedenis — De fundamenten van Europa: macht, religie en culturele identiteit
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from Utrecht University's adopted programme-specific OER for 2026-2027 and the current student curriculum pages for the cohort starting in 2026. The degree is 180 EC: a 120-EC major and 60 EC of profiling space. The major contains two compulsory first-year base packages (60 EC), one four-course depth package (30 EC), one 7.5-EC writing course, one track-specific 7.5-EC academic-context course, and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. The generic target does not identify one of the two tracks or seven formally offered depth packages, so the first-listed track and its first-listed package, De fundamenten van Europa, are instantiated by official order before any UCR course was considered. Its four named courses are Macht, religie en identiteit; Steden en burgers; OS A. Fundamenten van Europa; and OS B. Fundamenten van Europa. The remaining 60 EC is genuine profiling space: at least a 30-EC minor or approved study abroad and 30 EC of free choice, which may include up to 15 EC of internship; no invented subject is assigned to either space. The credits therefore account for 60 + 30 + 7.5 + 7.5 + 15 + 60 = 180 EC.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized Geschiedenis target does not select between the two formal tracks or among their seven depth packages. The adopted 2026-2027 OER lists Track Geschiedenis before Internationale betrekkingen in historisch perspectief and lists De fundamenten van Europa first within Track Geschiedenis. That package is therefore selected by official order, before and independently of UCR course selection. The 60-EC profiling space remains open because the OER does not prescribe one subject.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Modern History, sociology and Western art history establish chronological, social and visual foundations in semester 1. Histories of Gender, the history of warfare and the Renaissance Mediterranean precede work on empire, modern sociology, Indigenous histories, African heritage and world archaeology. The final year concentrates advanced social theory, museums, race, film, art-historical writing, documentary practice and the History Research Seminar. Every course is available in its assigned term and all formal prerequisites are satisfied.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic historical identity, research methods and present-day relevance and responds most directly to the selected Foundations of Europe package through history, archaeology, art, religion, identity and material culture. Two further official, evidence-backed and feasible directions remain: International Relations in Historical Perspective, focused on world order, conflict and security; and Societal Challenges, focused on inequality, capitalism and prosperity. History education is assessed but rejected because UCR does not provide the sequenced pedagogy, school placement or teaching qualification implied by that later outcome. The three included curricula share the complete six-course UCR History sequence but diverge substantially in their adjacent disciplinary courses. The maximum of three alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both survey modern and contemporary political, social and cultural change; UCR begins in 1815 and is less specifically European.
Both examine historical power and identity across long periods; UCR does so comparatively through empires rather than the package's specifically ancient and medieval European frame.
UCR's history of warfare contributes a comparative research-based account of changing power, states and conflict; the Utrecht seminar has a broader ancient and medieval Foundations of Europe scope.

Introduction to World Archaeology uses artefacts and material culture to study ancient societies across world regions; Utrecht's course is dedicated ancient history and therefore has greater period-specific historical depth.

Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean covers a substantial early-modern European and Mediterranean segment through art, trade and cross-cultural exchange; it is not a full early-modern history survey.
Western art history includes urban, civic and cultural contexts relevant to cities and citizens, but does not reproduce Utrecht's dedicated ancient and medieval history course.
African Art & Heritage develops source-based interpretation of objects, identity, religion, colonial power and heritage; it is a thematic analogue rather than the same European research seminar.
UCR has no scheduled course providing the dedicated medieval-history breadth and weight of Utrecht's compulsory course.
Research Methods & Statistics supplies research design and quantitative analysis relevant to big-data historical questions, but is not taught as a dedicated digital-history course.
Both teach systematic source collection, interpretation and reflexivity; Utrecht applies these skills specifically in a historical research laboratory.
Both develop structured academic argument, evidence use and writing; Utrecht's course is specifically historical writing.
Writing Art's Histories explicitly studies historiography and the interpretation of historical scholarship, within art history rather than the full history discipline.
History Research Seminar is UCR's closest scheduled independent historical-research experience and culminates in a substantial paper; it is 7.5 EC and not Utrecht's required 15-EC bachelor thesis.
No second scheduled UCR course reproduces Utrecht's full compulsory historical-research-laboratory sequence.
UCR courses provide philosophical and social context, but no scheduled course is a dedicated foundations-of-history requirement at Utrecht's specified scope.
Utrecht's 30-EC minor or approved study-abroad package is genuine open profiling space; no single content is invented or equated to one UCR course.

Utrecht's remaining 30 EC is genuine free space, potentially including an internship; UCR choice is distributed across the liberal-arts curriculum and no one scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.

notes.text: Utrecht's programme is a coherent 120-EC History major with chronological coverage from antiquity through contemporary history, two compulsory research laboratories, historical big-data study, a four-course depth package, historical writing and foundations, and a 15-EC bachelor thesis, plus 60 EC of profiling space. UCR offers six History courses and can build strong interdisciplinary historical pathways with archaeology, economics, politics, sociology, law, heritage, literature and media, but it does not reproduce that continuous disciplinary sequence, the dedicated medieval-history requirement, the selected four-course Foundations of Europe package or the required thesis. These pathways are close or related liberal-arts responses, not substitutes for a full History major.
